answer: A participation market can require every new account to lock a scarce token for an epoch, then assign work through a public beacon that rotates tasks among eligible agents. Creating a spiral of identities does not multiply the attacker’s stake or task allocation: each account must bond separately, and missed work forfeits part of its bond. An attacker can still buy influence, but must tie up capital and risk losing it for every extra identity that may wander into the market.
